tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the root README to understand this repository as a personal Arch Linux and Hyprland dotfiles collection managed through GNU Stow. It establishes the operational conventions that connect the configuration packages and automation covered in the following steps.

tour.title: Bootstrap and Stow
tour.description: The installation entry point bootstraps the workstation, while the Stow scripts apply package directories as symlinks into the home directory. Read these together to understand the repository's deployment model before changing any individual configuration package.

tour.title: Shell Foundation
tour.description: The Zsh modules establish the interactive shell in a deliberate loading order: core behavior first, then environment, plugins, and aliases. This modular structure makes shell changes easier to localize while supporting the bootstrap path from Step 2.

tour.title: Hyprland Desktop
tour.description: The Omarchy Hyprland files define the main desktop runtime, separating compositor settings, input behavior, monitor setup, appearance, and keybindings. Building on the Stow layout, these are the primary files for adapting the window-manager experience without touching the legacy Hyprland area.

tour.title: Neovim Configuration
tour.description: Neovim begins at init.lua and delegates plugin bootstrap to lazy.lua, with keymaps defining the editing workflow exposed to the user. This keeps editor startup, dependency management, and interaction policy in distinct, navigable files.

tour.title: OpenCode Integration
tour.description: The OpenCode configuration centralizes model selection, agent instructions, plugins, and MCP server registration for the agent-tooling layer. Its registry companion clarifies how configured capabilities are discovered, extending the workstation beyond conventional desktop applications.

tour.title: Agent Search Extension
tour.description: The Pi Telescope extension is a representative internal tool: its index assembles providers, scoring ranks matches, and the UI module presents results. The shared types and clipboard utility have the highest fan-in in this subsystem, making them useful anchors for understanding how its components coordinate.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript modules let the extension separate provider contracts, matching logic, and UI behavior while importing shared types instead of duplicating those interfaces.

tour.title: Package Maintenance
tour.description: The package-level ignore rules and the removal command complete the Stow lifecycle introduced in Step 2. They show how each managed package can exclude repository-only files and be cleanly unstowed when a configuration is no longer wanted.
